shared_context.content: For integers m >= 2 and h >= 0, K_{m,h} is the set of tuples x=(x_1,...,x_{m-1}) of positive integers such that x_1+...+x_{m-1}=h and, for all i,j in {1,...,m-1}, if i+j < m then x_i+x_j >= x_{i+j}, while if i+j > m then x_i+x_j+1 >= x_{i+j-m}.
shared_context.label: K_definition

shared_context.content: For x in K_{m,g} and r in {1,...,m-1}, write x+e_r for the tuple obtained by increasing the r-th coordinate by 1 and leaving all other coordinates unchanged. The one-step increment graph G_{m,g} has left part K_{m,g}, right part K_{m,g+1}, and edges x~y exactly when y=x+e_r for some r.
shared_context.label: increment_graph

shared_context.content: Lexicographic order on tuples in Z^{m-1}: x <_lex y if, at the first coordinate where x and y differ, the tuple x has the smaller entry.
shared_context.label: lex_order

strategy_summary: Build the bipartite graph whose left vertices are tuples in K_{m,g}, whose right vertices are tuples in K_{m,g+1}, and whose edges correspond to increasing exactly one coordinate by 1. Prove Hall's condition for this graph by a lexicographic compression principle: among all left subsets of a fixed size, lexicographic initial segments have the smallest neighborhoods, and every such initial segment has at least as many neighbors as vertices. Hall's marriage theorem then gives the desired injection.
